messages:
devon: quick heads-up — after kernel-chooser v2.4 rolled, we're seeing a perf regression on qwen2.5 for short multilang requests. median seq ~18 tokens, p99 latency up ~22%. i think it's kernel handoff + KV-cache fragmentation from tokenizer subtokens.

devon: minimal profile from canary (consumer load):
```
kernel_switches: 72
kv_evictions: 14
kv_hits_pct: 82.3
mean_latency_ms: 28.1
p50: 20.3
p95: 62.5
p99: 85.2  # baseline was ~70
cpu memcpy_ms: +9%
```

arya: @devon thanks. that kernel_switches number stands out. autokernel probably switches mid-request when it detects kv/head dim mismatch. can you run with `kernel_selector=fast_smallseq` pinned and `batch_window_ms=12` to see if it stabilizes? also collect kv cache hit histogram and per-token kernel id.

matt: repro'd on eu-canary. autokernel picked `matmul_fused` for attention when heads=96 but kv_head_dim=64 triggers the fallback execution path after kv cache materialization -> extra memcpy + memcpy sync. setting `kernel_selector=legacy_for_kv_mismatch` drops p99 back ~9ms.

sasha: another angle — tokenizer fragmentation. mixed zh/en inputs produce lots of tiny subtokens and frequent prefix boundary changes, which reduces prefix reuse in KV cache. i dumped some tokenization examples: many tokens are single-char CJK + subsequent english subtokens -> frequent kv boundary splits. might be inflating eviction rate.

devon: good catches. proposed action: (1) add a shortseq perf test for qwen2.5 that mirrors the observed token distribution, (2) change kernel selector to avoid mid-request kernel handoff (no in-flight switch), (3) experiment with ropescale tweaks for qwen2.5 when head_dim!=kv_head_dim to avoid fallback path. example override we can try: `--runtime-override 'kernel_selector=fast_smallseq;allow_runtime_switch=false;ropescale_override=0.8'`.

arya: also collect `kv_cache_prefix_length` histogram and `kernel_id_per_token` trace. those will show whether the cache is being reused or repeatedly rebuilt. add an alert if `kv_evictions/sec > 5` on shortseq workloads.

bench-bot: queued bench-suite/qwen2p5/shortseq on canary (bs-id: 2423). will post structured results here when done. :rocket:

matt: if bench confirms, i'll send a small rollback patch for kernel-chooser and follow up with a targeted experiment to detect `heads != kv_heads` and force the legacy path for qwen2.5 until we have a proper fused path.

sasha: also worth trying a token merge heuristic: `tokenizer.tune_merge_threshold=0.65` for mixed-language inputs, see if kv reuse improves. small A/B on canary should be cheap.

devon: +1. i'll open a short RFC and link repro scripts. thanks all — tagging @arya/matt for follow-ups.
